intent: The borderless text input that sits among the chips of a multiple-value Combobox and takes the query that filters the list.
typical_uses: The query input at the end of ComboboxChips

dont_use_when.situation: The field of a one-value combobox

invariants.text: Backspace in the empty input removes the last chosen value, and the arrow key toward the chips (left, or right in a right-to-left layout) at the start of the input moves focus onto the last chip.
The input draws no border, background or focus ring; the enclosing ComboboxChips draws them for the whole field.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave the input with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible label; the placeholder is not a name

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, popupSide, listEmpty, readOnly, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

good.title: The query input after the chips
good.code:
<ComboboxChips ref={anchor}>
  <ComboboxValue>
    {(values) => values.map((value) => <ComboboxChip key={value}>{value}</ComboboxChip>)}
  </ComboboxValue>
  <ComboboxChipsInput aria-label="Frameworks" placeholder="Add a framework" />
</ComboboxChips>

bad.title: The chips input used as a one-value field
bad.why: Without ComboboxChips around it the input has no border, background or focus ring, so it draws as bare text; a one-value field is ComboboxInput.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxInputState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ComboboxInputState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the input's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, popupSide, listEmpty, readOnly, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
